answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a relic as the anchor of the cost. A summit stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a thread hold...
